title: Mass Gatherings

source.boundary: Start at actual Mass Gatherings title in lower left column of page 13, then continue in right column. Exclude Chapter 3 text above title in left column. End at references on page 18, the final page of this section PDF.
source.verification: Selected vocabulary occurrence and chapter boundaries, not clinical guidance, legal advice or source entailment of a proposed metaphor.

scope: Sixteen selected terms, not exhaustive chapter coverage. Offline candidate associations, not clinical narration or renderer prompts. Existing chapter cues explicitly reused rather than counted as new.

entries.cue: Large crowd clustered together at an event.
entries.reason: Literal familiar category is useful without forced wordplay. Does not encode an attendance threshold or define event risk by crowd size alone.

entries.cue: Doctor in a film director's chair holding a clapperboard.
entries.reason: Familiar director role supplies a memorable double meaning. No operational command authority, qualifications or legal duties inferred from the prop.

entries.cue: Scout with binoculars examining a venue map.
entries.reason: Binoculars and venue context provide a useful scouting association; not a complete inspection checklist or security assessment.

entries.cue: Medic sheltered beneath an oversized shield.
entries.reason: Provider plus protection is appropriate at category level. Does not specify protective equipment, threats or actual protection capabilities.

entries.cue: Commander at a conspicuous control console.
entries.reason: Familiar role and tool link the phrase. Does not encode the Incident Command System hierarchy, personnel assignments or authoritative operating procedures.

entries.cue: A large tree with branching chutes sorting patient tokens into separate groups.
entries.reason: A learned tree/sorting bridge rather than exact phonetics. No age-based prioritization, color categories, severity criteria or fixed algorithm is implied. Only a few large groups needed for legibility.

entries.cue: Charcoal briquette superhero with a prominent illuminated power-button symbol.
entries.reason: Anthropomorphism and activation cue supply the name. Activation is wordplay, not electricity as the real activation process; no poisoning indication, preparation or therapeutic claim.

entries.cue: Ant holding an acid bottle with a familiar corrosive pictogram.
entries.reason: Simple near-sound assembly. Bottle identity can be taught through the familiar corrosive symbol without printing the answer. Not ingesting acid, a neutralization diagram or evidence for a particular drug's effects.

entries.cue: Conspicuous stop barrier across a recognizable vomiting bucket.
entries.reason: A learned prevention/category association can work without spelling every syllable. Not a specific medication, recommendation, guarantee of benefit or clinical mechanism.

entries.cue: Astronaut wrapped in a shiny foil blanket.
entries.reason: Familiar astronaut and reflective blanket combine the words. No insulation rating, treatment or aerospace-material claim.

entries.cue: Sturdy box containing conspicuous needle shapes.
entries.reason: Literal familiar equipment category is sufficient. This is a standalone token, not a demonstration of safe disposal, filling levels or recapping.

entries.cue: Parrot perched on a recognizable antenna.
entries.reason: Familiar repetition association need not show sound waves or a temporal sequence. Not an explanation of radio technology or coverage performance.
User's earlier retained association, reused for consistency rather than inventing another symbol. Not a physiological mechanism or clinical sign.

entries.cue: Dynamite stick as the learned nitro token.
entries.cue_scope: Drug identity token in lesson context
entries.reason: Reuses the Chapter 2 candidate, not a new discovery. No medicinal formulation, handling hazard or therapeutic effect claim.

entries.cue: Recognizable blood-pressure cuff with squeeze bulb and dial.
entries.reason: The real device silhouette is a valid vocabulary cue; no forced long-word rebus required. Learner may retrieve blood-pressure cuff before the formal name, which can be explicitly taught. No measurement threshold or technique.

entries.cue_scope: No new economical identity cue established
entries.reason: No convincing proposal in this bounded pass. Do not fabricate syllable fragments or substitute generic medication imagery simply to increase yield.
